return_value.derivation: The epilogue block 0x004D251F has exactly one predecessor: the fall-through of block 0x004D2504-0x004D251F, whose only conditional edge is 0x004D2519 jl 0x004D2392. That block starts 0x004D2504 mov eax,dword [esp+0x24] (the loop counter), then 0x004D2510 cmp eax,0x800, 0x004D2515 mov [esp+0x24],eax, 0x004D2519 jl. The loop is entered with [esp+0x24]=0 at 0x004D2386 and incremented by 1 at 0x004D250B, so it exits only with EAX = 0x800. No instruction between 0x004D2504 and the retn writes EAX.
return_value.what_0x800_is: 0x800 = 2048 = the iteration count and the terminating value of the final loop, which walks 28-byte (0x1C) records based at 0x00B04340. The same 2048 bound appears as the hash mask 0x7FF at 0x004D214C (and eax,0x7ff), and the stride 28 is computed at 0x004D2113-0x004D211C (lea ecx,[eax*8] ; sub ecx,eax ; shl ecx,2). 2048 * 0x1C = 0xE000, i.e. 0x00B04340-0x00B12340. The returned value is therefore the size of the previous-frame cache table that the function scans, not a data-dependent result.
return_value.caller_use: discarded at the only call site (see callers[0].return_use)

base_case: No root at all: 0x4D1860 test eax,eax ; 0x4D1862 je 0x4D1882 skips the only block that initialises [esp+0x240] and [esp+0x244] (0x4D186D, 0x4D1877). On that path the five-child loop reads [esp+0x244] as its mask accumulator at 0x4D18CC and the DFS entry block reads the same dword at 0x4D1A42 before any stack-depth comparison. This is an uninitialised stack read in the retail code, recorded as an instruction-level observation and not as intended behaviour; a transcription must decide deliberately whether to reproduce it.
Empty stack: the pop path leaves esi = base-8 so 0x4D2321 jae fails and control falls to 0x4D2327.
Leaf record with no child mask: 0x4D1C3B cmp eax,ecx (mask vs 0) ; 0x4D1C43 je 0x4D1D33.
Mask bit not set for the current child: 0x4D1C6C test eax,edi ; 0x4D1C6E je 0x4D1D13.
No descend bits in the key: 0x4D1A82 test eax,eax ; 0x4D1A84 je 0x4D1B74.
Null child node in the five-child loop: 0x4D18AF test edx,edx ; 0x4D18B1 je 0x4D19A3.
Null record in the write-back loop: 0x4D233C test edi,edi ; 0x4D233E je 0x4D2349.
iteration_order: Child selection is an ascending bit scan: the bit register starts at 1 and doubles per iteration (0x4D1B58 shl eax,0x1 and 0x4D1D1A shl eax,0x1), over the 5-bit mask tested at 0x4D1B50/0x4D1C6C.

The five child slots are the entries of the byte table at 0x00548444 = {0,1,2,4,5}; slot 3 is not used by either loop (0x4D1887 mov esi,0x00548444 ; 0x4D1895 sub esi,0xA gives the base 0x0054843A used at 0x4D18A7 with index 0xA..0xE, i.e. 0x00548444..0x00548448; 0x4D2331 reads 0x00548444+0..4).
Within a record, the eight child slots are indexed by (key >> 7) & 7 (0x4D1A49 sar edx,0x7 ; 0x4D1A4C and edx,0x7) into the dword array at [record+0xC] (0x4D1C7A mov eax,dword [eax+edx*4+0xC]).

The eight-corner inner loop (L12) visits corners in the order given by eight consecutive bytes read from [esp+0x1C0 + 8*row] (0x4D1DD2 lea ecx,[esp+eax*8+0x1C0] ; 0x4D1E31 movsx ecx,byte [eax] ; 0x4D1E34 inc eax). That 64-byte table is built at 0x4D15B8..0x4D15FC from the low byte of each dword of the 64-dword table at 0x00548060, which is eight rows of eight distinct values 0..7.
traversal_structure.quaternary_versus_octary: The instructions show a 3-bit, 8-slot child array ([record+0xC] with (key>>7)&7) and an 8-corner inner loop, while the two outer loops use only five of the eight slots (table {0,1,2,4,5}). 'Quadtree' is only the Binary Ninja annotation. This record does not assert a branching factor for the data structure.

facts: 0x004D14E0 is 4181 bytes (0x004D14E0-0x004D2534 inclusive), with one ret at 0x004D2525 and 11 bytes of 0x90 padding before 0x004D2540.
The function has 146 basic blocks, 228 edges, 1114 instructions, 83 conditional jumps, 13 jmp, 6 call instructions and 4 rep movsd.
It uses cdecl and reads exactly one 4-byte stack argument at [ebp+0x8], at three sites.
Its only caller is 0x004D2639 inside 0x004D2540, which pushes exactly one dword.
It has one ret and EAX at that ret is provably 0x800 = 2048, the terminating value of the loop that scans 2048 28-byte records based at 0x00B04340.
It is not self-recursive in the binary; the traversal uses an explicit 8-byte-per-entry LIFO at [esp+0x240].

When arg1->[0x0C] is null, the only block that initialises the DFS frame ([esp+0x240], [esp+0x244]) is skipped (0x4D1862 je 0x4D1882), yet [esp+0x244] is still read as the mask accumulator at 0x4D18CC and as the frame key at 0x4D1A42. The retail code therefore reads uninitialised stack memory on that path. Recorded as an instruction-level fact; no meaning is assigned to it.
Two calls go through zero-filled pointer tables at 0x00A9CAE0 and 0x00A9C4E0, selected by a 16-bit word at [item+0x1C]; their targets are not in the file image.
The five child slots come from the byte table at 0x00548444 = {0,1,2,4,5}, applied to [arg1+0x10+4*idx].
The 0x40-byte record mask byte at +0x30 is bit-reversed in place, and eight dwords at +0x0C..+0x28 are written in reverse order from the scratch copy.
The three error paths call Debug_Error and then spin on 'jmp $' instead of returning.

limitations: Static analysis only for everything outside the runtime section. No transcription, build, structural or runtime verification of any implementation exists; status stays ANALYZED.

No paired retail and candidate evidence exists for this function. The candidate for this VA is a placeholder that throws, so there is nothing to compare against; no differential capture was made and none is claimed.
The runtime numbers come from a single retail-only capture with a late attach, so startup calls are missing and 1244 is a from-attach count.
The runtime argument words beyond the first are caller stack residue; they are recorded as captured but must not be read as arguments.
The two indirect callees cannot be resolved from the image: 0x00A9CAE0 and 0x00A9C4E0 are in the zero-filled tail of .data (beyond the 0x1A000 raw bytes) and hold zeros on disk.

Binary Ninja symbol names (Terrain_TraverseContourQuadtree, Render_DrawLightmapMesh_4, DynObj_ParseConfigFile_6, Debug_Error, g_xxx) are database annotations, not retail symbols. The 0x004C5810 name in particular is contradicted by its own body.

The x87 conversions (ten 'fistp qword' sites in this function: 0x4D1500, 0x4D1631, 0x4D1651, 0x4D1683, 0x4D171F, 0x4D1737, 0x4D1743, 0x4D1818, 0x4D182E, 0x4D183D; plus 0x4D261C in the caller) store 64-bit integers but only the low dword is consumed, and the conversion truncates or rounds according to the current x87 control word, which this function does not set. Any reconstruction must reproduce the caller's rounding mode; that is an assumption here, not a verified fact.
The meaning of the cube record bytes 0x000-0x00B, 0x020, 0x034 and 0x03C-0x047 is not established, and no meaning is invented for them.
The overlap between the node slot at +0x00C (0x4D197D) and slot 0 of the child array at +0x00C (0x4D1C7A) is recorded as unresolved rather than guessed.

The 8-corner inner loop's row index register ([esp+0x10]) also accumulates flag bits on some paths (0x4D2009 sets a 0x400 bit); the exact reachable value range at 0x4D1DD2 was not proven, so the row indexing is described by instruction, not by asserted range.

Prior evidence files for this VA (0x004D14E0-binaryninja.json, -radare2.json, -build.json, -behavioral.json, -semantic-review.json) contain only CFG node/edge dumps and build/behaviour labels with no argument or return semantics; nothing was copied from them, and every fact here was re-derived from the binary and the capture files.

No candidate build was executed, no call was compared across the two programs, and no return value, memory effect or ordering has been shown equivalent.
